audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer phases[N].side read a blanket 'Skill' while content win[0..3] are 'Xerath' and win[4..6] are 'Skill' — which is exactly the packet levelChart. The two layers disagreed on the first four rows.
audit.why: Xerath's W (1000) and E (1050) outrange Zoe's Q (800) and Sleepy Trouble Bubble (800), and his poke is point-fire while hers needs a two-part skillshot; levels 1-4 are his. From 6 Portal Jump (11/8/5s) plus a charged Paddle Star! kills a squishy exactly as Rite of the Arcane does, so those rows really are skill.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side to Xerath; phases[4..6] stay Skill, with the Xerath-flavoured whys on rows 4, 5 and 6 rewritten so the sentence stops arguing with a Skill verdict.

audit.why: Lost Chapter, level 6 and Luden's are the right beats; the level 6 row is genuinely shared because both ultimates convert a chipped squishy into a kill.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never states what Sleep actually does: Riot's text says the target's magic resist is reduced while asleep and the first source of damage that breaks the sleep is doubled, up to a cap. The page also omitted Portal Jump's numbers (11/8/5s, 575 range, blinks back after 1 second) — the tempo tool that decides whether her poke is answerable.
audit.why: Doubling the wake-up hit and shredding MR is why one Sleep ends an immobile Xerath, and the blink-back is why chasing her poke with a 13s stun fails. Both are the load-bearing facts of the matchup and neither reached a field.
audit.corrected: Both written into breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull[0].d and dontsFull[2].d with the real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: It is the field that exists to hold real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with Sleepy Trouble Bubble 18/17/16/15/14s at 800 range and Portal Jump 11/8/5s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabricated-adjacent ability names: spikes[0].text and wants.foe[1] both write 'Paddle Star' / 'Paddle Stars' where Riot's name is 'Paddle Star!' with the exclamation mark (packet defects, suspectNames, distance 1).
audit.why: The packet flagged them as probable wrong names and the kit confirms the real one.

audit.whatIsWrong: Zoe is female and 20 fields addressed her as he/his/him (lint MISGENDER x18 plus the two carried into report copies). Separately dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim under unrelated titles (COPY_PASTE_BLEED x2), and tradeBad referenced 'the dash' — Zoe's only mobility is a blink that returns her to where she started.
audit.why: champ-data/champ-gender.js lists zoe as female; the owner is addressed as 'you', so every third-person pronoun on the page is Zoe.
audit.corrected: Every flagged field repronouned, and the two bled bullets rewritten to their own titles.

audit.why: matchup-lint reported MISGENDER / COPY_PASTE_BLEED / COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT / UNSUPPORTED_MAGNITUDE / HEDGING on these fields; cooldowns and ranges taken from champ-data/_kits.
audit.corrected: Pronouns matched to the enemy champion; bled trade text replaced with field-specific advice; cooldown lines given real per-rank numbers.

notes: content win[0..6] already matched the packet exactly (Xerath x4 then Skill x3), so the full-layer side flips are unpaired by design — before==after win[N] edits would be no-ops and would take the atomic chart group down. phases[4], [5] and [6] keep side 'Skill' but their whys were rewritten in this same proposal because all three described Xerath winning a stage the row calls even. DATA DEFECT to fix upstream: champ-data/_kits/zoe.json flags Sleepy Trouble Bubble as 'trueDamage' and 'terrain'. Riot's own description says the target's magic resist is reduced and the first damage that breaks the sleep is doubled up to a cap — that is amplified magic damage, not true damage, and no terrain is created. Both flags misfired, and the _missing 'resistances-invalidated' headline for this matchup derives from the trueDamage flag, so I wrote no edit asserting MR is worthless against Zoe. The 'More Sparkles!' auto-reset tell from _missing is real and correct but I could not place it inside the length band without displacing a cooldown number, so it is unplaced. tradeGood/tradeBad appear verbatim in breakdown.trading and report[3]; all three were edited together so the copies stay identical.
